video.title: The Massive Machine Hidden in the Deep Ocean

protocol.status: v2 labeler B (rubric v2), independent of A
protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Mystery: 900 balls strung up off Sicily, a computer in an abandoned winery watching them; in 2023 something smaller than an electron set off a signal 30x more powerful than ever seen, telescopes swing to look and 'they find... nothing.' Lands on 'nothing' at 63.1; 'scientists are searching for answers' to 69.9 is acceptable. Cannot start at the 2023 line: it opens 'And ... they'.

Analogy with a reveal: fly to the next star (40 trillion km, 75,000 years, 'a lot of space in space'); shrink to a tiny particle and solid rock is just as empty -- 'that is what it's like to be a neutrino'. Lands at 161.4; the millimeter-neutrino / human-as-galaxy scale line to 173.9 is acceptable. Starts right after the AT&T credit.

Surprising fact: every ~10 seconds a star somewhere goes supernova; these explosions make the silicon, oxygen and iron in planets and us -- 'the iron in your blood can be traced back to a supernova', lands at 337.4. Continuing to 'neutrinos are your messenger' (355.2) also works and adds the video's point, so both ends are acceptable. Starts after 'So, for example,'.

Explanation: the neutrino hits a proton, making a particle that 'flies through the water faster than light'; nothing beats light in a vacuum but light slows in water, so the particle leaves a cone -- 'is it like a sonic boom?' 'exactly like a sonic boom', a flash of blue light instead of a boom. Lands at 625.3.

Discovery story: in 2017 a neutrino tears through Antarctic ice, telescopes swing and find a blazar four billion light years away; only the neutrino confirmed it as a cosmic engine, source of heavy metals and cosmic rays. Lands at 818-820.6; 'the beginning of a whole new era in astronomy' to 833.4 also works.

Discovery: in 2022 IceCube found an active galaxy whose core was hidden by gas and dust; light couldn't escape, 'but neutrinos could, and did' -- the first look inside a cosmic engine light could never show us, at 869.8. The expert's 'watershed moment' quote to 879.2 is acceptable.

also_ok.why: 'From the little neutrino's perspective': born in a supernova, a dull billion years in a straight line, then by chance it hits 'some poor proton' in water off Sicily; 100 trillion through you a second, so statistically some hit. Charming, but what the hit produces comes in the next clip.

Filtering out bioluminescence and particles from above by looking only at what passed through the Earth: 'think of it as the back of a giant telescope, where the lens is the entire Earth'. Opens on 'this computer ... this special blue light', so acceptable, not insisted on.

negatives.why: 'How do you catch one? You build a very big and very crazy machine' -- the question is really answered minutes later.
Building a DOM by hand in the lab, 'pay attention to the air bubbles', 'he's checking my work': a room/demo moment.
Single-photon sensitivity, 'like hearing a single drop on a single leaf in a hurricane': vivid, but 'each one' points at the screen and it is a fragment.
'This is what KM3NeT sees, and this is what IceCube sees': narration of a graphic.
'Just look at this, nearly a thousand scientists on this paper': screen reference.
Subscribe call and AT&T sponsor credit.
